info.summary: Complete short story • A needle and a thread argue over work, pride and recognition
info.translationCredit: Portuguese: Machado de Assis (died 1908). Várias Histórias, Rio de Janeiro: Laemmert & C., 1896, pp. 253–257; complete individual short story, not the entire collection. Preserved the Wikisource transcription’s spelling. Separated the needle’s speech from the following narrative paragraph; corrected the joined words “linhaordinária” to “linha ordinária”; normalized whitespace. No prose omitted. Study note: mucamas is a historical term for domestic female attendants, often enslaved women in nineteenth-century Brazil; the English “maids” names their household role without implying free employment. Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt; the speaking needle and thread are a satire on who does the work and who receives the rewards.
